design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable single-clock FPGA control-and-safety top for host-managed surrogate execution in an automotive aerodynamics context. The design implements firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control and status, compact 128-bit request/response transport, validation, sequence tracking, watchdog timeout handling, safety gating, and registered actuator command outputs without instantiating the surrogate model in RTL.
design_summary.operating_model: A host or CPU prepares model-side content externally, then exchanges compact request and response packets with the FPGA. The FPGA validates protocol metadata, tracks sequence and freshness policy, manages watchdog timing, clamps accepted command values within programmed bounds, and either forwards a registered actuator command when all checks pass or suppresses command validity and latches faults for software handling. All externally visible outputs are registered and synchronous to the single clk domain.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.intent: Single synchronous clock domain input for the full design.

external_interfaces.name: rst_n
external_interfaces.intent: Active-low reset input for deterministic safe initialization.

external_interfaces.name: req_ready
external_interfaces.intent: FPGA backpressure/acceptance indication for the request stream.

external_interfaces.name: rsp_ready
external_interfaces.intent: Host backpressure on the response stream.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level FPGA control-and-safety block for host-managed aerodynamic surrogate operation.
responsibilities: Expose the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface and the 128-bit request/response transport.
Decode compact request packets containing opcode, sequence number, freshness/age, target, bounds index, and integrity metadata.
Validate opcode, sequence ordering, freshness/age, packet length indicators, and integrity metadata.
Maintain minimal sequence/watchdog state and a single in-flight command shadow.
Clamp accepted command values to programmable minimum and maximum bounds before forward propagation.
Assert and latch protocol, stale, timeout, and clamp-related status for software observability.
Prevent unsafe actuator command output after timeout or any validation failure by suppressing command validity and latching faults.
Keep all externally visible outputs registered and synchronous.
Avoid instantiating the surrogate model in RTL.
Remain deterministic and amenable to formal verification of safety and timeout behavior.
interface_notes: Top-level ports are limited to clk, rst_n, the streaming transport, CSR/MMIO, and actuator command interfaces.
No vehicle geometry arrays, flow fields, pressure maps, or model tensors are exposed at the top level.
A top-level output is driven by real RTL logic and not left to a child input-only path.
ownership_notes: This module owns the top-level integration point and delegates CSR decode to adaptive_aero_control_csr and protocol/safety transport to adaptive_aero_control_transport.
The top does not redefine hierarchy or ports.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_csr
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decode and register block.
responsibilities: Decode the 32-bit, 6-bit-address control/status window.
Store configuration for enable, sequence policy, stale threshold, watchdog limit, minimum and maximum bounds, default mode, and sticky-fault clear control.
Return readable status for mode, sequence, watchdog, and fault indicators.
Provide ready/acknowledge semantics for CSR transactions.
Clear sticky faults when commanded by firmware through the CSR interface.
Ensure every declared register is reachable through decode logic.
interface_notes: Inputs include csr_valid, csr_write, csr_addr, csr_wdata, clk, rst_n, and status feedback from transport.

Outputs include csr_rdata, csr_ready, and semantic configuration fields cfg_enable, cfg_enforce_sequence, cfg_stale_threshold, cfg_watchdog_limit, cfg_min_bound, cfg_max_bound, cfg_default_mode, and cfg_clear_sticky.
Status inputs are read-only mirrors of transport state and are not directly writable.
ownership_notes: This module owns software-visible configuration and status ownership.
It implements the register_contract described in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON, including CTRL, STALENESS, WATCHDOG, BOUNDS_MIN, BOUNDS_MAX, DEFAULT_MODE, STATUS, SEQ, and WD.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_transport
module_architecture.role: Protocol and safety transport engine for 128-bit request and response packets.
responsibilities: Consume host request packets and emit host response packets.
Validate request opcode, sequence ordering, freshness/age, length, integrity metadata, and heartbeat/session management.
Track one in-flight request shadow and manage watchdog state.
Generate compact response records with acknowledgment, fault codes, watchdog status, and command summary.
Drive registered actuator command outputs only when the request is accepted and the safety policy permits propagation.
Latch protocol, stale, clamp, and timeout faults according to policy.
Use only minimal control metadata and one in-flight shadow, with optional technology-neutral BRAM-mappable payload/history buffering when required.
Suppress command validity on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions without substituting a fallback command.
interface_notes: Consumes req_valid, req_data, rsp_ready, cfg_enable, cfg_enforce_sequence, cfg_stale_threshold, cfg_watchdog_limit, cfg_min_bound, cfg_max_bound, cfg_default_mode, cfg_clear_sticky, and payload_mem_dout.

Drives req_ready, rsp_valid, rsp_data, status_mode, status_last_sequence, status_watchdog_count, status_stale_fault, status_timeout_fault, status_clamp_fault, status_protocol_fault, status_safe_active, cmd_valid, cmd_value, cmd_mode, cmd_fault, cmd_safe, payload_mem_csb, payload_mem_we, payload_mem_addr, and payload_mem_din.
The request-valid/request-ready handshake governs acceptance; no implicit acceptance occurs.
Output registration is preserved at the transport boundary.
ownership_notes: This module owns the real-time safety decisions for transport acceptance and command gating.
It is the source of the actuator command outputs that the top-level ports expose.

module_architecture.name: fpga_bram_generic
module_architecture.role: Technology-neutral memory macro abstraction for optional payload/history buffering.
responsibilities: Expose the declared memory macro interface for RTL generation and downstream FPGA collateral.
Provide a BRAM-mappable storage abstraction if compact transport buffering or history is required.
Avoid describing or storing model tensors, vehicle geometry, or large bulk payloads as registers.
interface_notes: The abstraction uses clk, payload_mem_csb, payload_mem_we, payload_mem_addr, payload_mem_din, and payload_mem_dout.
It is a single-port memory macro interface and is not a software-visible register block.
The memory contents are not reset by controller reset.
ownership_notes: This module is the technology-neutral wrapper for the memory_macros entry named fpga_bram_generic.
It is meant for FPGA inference to native block RAM and does not represent a Sky130 hard macro in FPGA synthesis.

interface_summary.intent: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO transactions are decoded and read back through the CSR block.
Host transport and registered actuator command behavior are implemented in the transport engine and exposed at the top level.
CSR-programmed policy, bounds, and sticky-fault control configure the transport and safety logic.
Transport state and sticky/observability indicators are mirrored back into the firmware-visible register block.
Optional technology-neutral payload/history buffering is connected through the BRAM abstraction.

data_flow_summary: The host supplies compact 128-bit request packets on req_data with req_valid, and the transport returns acceptance readiness on req_ready.
The transport decodes packet metadata, applies opcode and policy checks, evaluates sequence ordering and freshness, and uses CSR-programmed bounds and watchdog parameters.
Accepted commands are clamped within the configured bounds before a registered actuator command is emitted.

Fault conditions such as malformed packet content, stale age, unsupported opcode, sequence violations, or timeout suppress command validity and populate status and response fields for software handling.
The CSR block is the only firmware-visible register interface and reflects current mode, sequence, watchdog, and fault state while accepting configuration writes.
Optional BRAM-mapped buffering, if used, remains a narrow transport/history abstraction and is not a bulk model or geometry store.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain only, using clk at the documented 50.0 MHz operating point. All externally visible outputs are registered and no combinational loops or latches are introduced.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low and synchronous. On reset, safety state initializes to safe values, command outputs are invalid, safe-state indication is asserted, faults are cleared or set to their reset-defined state, sequence tracking is reset to a deterministic baseline, watchdog state is cleared, and CSR readback returns reset-defined defaults. No actuation command is asserted during reset or immediately after reset release until a valid request/session is accepted.

integration_notes: Digital control-plane integration is firmware-visible through the CSR/MMIO window; streaming transport does not replace this interface.

The request/response transport follows the mandatory direction contract: the RTL emits req_ready and rsp_valid/rsp_data, receives req_valid/req_data and rsp_ready, and keeps top-level outputs actively driven by RTL logic.
The design is descriptive-only here and inherits hierarchy, ports, and filenames from DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON without alteration.
Bulk payload/history storage, if required, is described through the fpga_bram_generic abstraction so FPGA flow can map it to native block RAM.

The top-level contract for automotive aerodynamics is host-managed surrogate execution; the RTL does not instantiate the surrogate model and does not expose geometry or model tensors at the top level.
No silent fallback command is introduced on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions; command validity is deasserted and faults are latched for software handling.
The register_contract is the authoritative software-visible map and all declared registers are reachable through RTL decode.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
